transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I just can’t seem to sit still when I’m supposed to. Like in the radiology suite, or even in class, I get this feeling like I’m crawling out of my skin if I have to stay in one place too long. It’s not just being a little bored or uncomfortable — it feels like this pressure building up in my body, and I end up shifting around constantly, pacing if I can, or making up some excuse to move.

I’ve been trying to just tough it out for months, telling myself to deal with it or that I should be able to control it, but I still end up needing to move. It’s getting hard to ignore, and I figured I should probably talk to someone instead of just pretending it’s fine.
When you feel that pressure building up and need to move, does moving actually relieve the feeling, or does it only help a little?

It does help, yeah — not like it fixes it completely, but it’s almost like letting steam out or something. If I’m sitting there in the radiology suite or in class and I’m trying to force myself to stay still, that crawling-out-of-my-skin feeling just keeps building. Like my legs want to go before I even decide to move.

So when I shift around, or stand up, or pace for a minute, it takes the edge off. It’s not even always that I have somewhere to go — sometimes I’m basically looking for a reason to move, like checking something, grabbing something, adjusting something that probably doesn’t need adjusting. And then I can breathe a little easier for a bit.

But it doesn’t last long if I have to sit back down. It comes right back, and after months of trying to just tough it out, I still end up doing it anyway.
Do you feel this same need to move and the crawling sensation in other places besides the radiology suite and class, like when you're at home or in other situations where you have to sit still?

Yeah, it’s mostly when I’m supposed to sit still, wherever that is. The radiology suite and the classroom are the big ones because that’s where it’s most obvious and where I’m expected to just stay put, but it’s not like the feeling only exists there.

It’s that same kind of crawling-out-of-my-skin thing — like my body is telling me to get up even when I’m trying to make myself stay seated. I’ll start shifting around, moving my legs, changing position over and over, and if I can get away with it I’ll pace or find some excuse to stand up. It’s almost embarrassing because sometimes I know I don’t actually need to go do anything, but I feel like I have to move anyway.

I’ve been trying for months to just tough it out and sit through it, but I still end up doing the same thing — shifting, pacing, or making up a reason to move around.
Do you ever feel that crawling sensation or need to move even when you're not in a situation where you're expected to sit still, like when you're relaxing at home or lying in bed?

Mostly it’s when I’m expected to sit still. Like, that’s where I really notice it — in the radiology suite or in class, when I’m supposed to just stay in one spot and pay attention or wait or not be distracting.

At home, if I’m able to get up whenever I want, it doesn’t feel as trapped, I guess. I might still move around, but it’s not the same because nobody’s making me sit there. The worst part is when I know I’m supposed to stay seated, and then that crawling-out-of-my-skin feeling starts building, and I’m trying to tell myself, “Just sit still, just deal with it,” but then I’m shifting around over and over, or I end up pacing, or I find some excuse to get up even if I don’t really need to.

So I wouldn’t say it’s only one place, but it’s definitely tied to situations where I’m supposed to stay still. That’s been going on for months, and I kept thinking I could just tough it out, but I still keep ending up needing to move.
Have you ever felt restless or found yourself moving without meaning to, even when you weren’t trying to sit still or were in a situation where you could move freely?

I mean… not really in the same way, I don’t think. If I’m somewhere I can move freely, it’s harder to tell, because I just do move. Like I’ll get up, shift around, pace a little, find something to adjust or check, and it doesn’t stand out as much because nobody’s telling me I have to stay seated.

The reason I came in is more because when I’m supposed to sit still — like in the radiology suite or in class — it feels awful, like I’m crawling out of my skin. I’ll try to tough it out, and I’ve been trying for months, but eventually I’m bouncing my leg, changing positions, pacing if I can, or making up some excuse to get up. It’s like the pressure builds until I move.

So if I’m not being forced to sit still, I may still be moving around, but I notice it way less. It’s the “you have to stay put” situations where it becomes really obvious and hard to control.

When you're trying to sit still, like in the radiology suite or in class, do you feel an actual urge or need to move your legs — not just boredom or discomfort, but like your legs are uncomfortable in a way that makes you need to move them?

Yeah… I think so, but it’s hard for me to separate whether it’s specifically my legs or just my whole body feeling like I need to move.

When I’m in the radiology suite or sitting in class and I’m supposed to stay still, it’s not just, “Oh, I’m bored.” It feels more physical than that, like I’m crawling out of my skin. My legs are usually the first thing that starts moving — bouncing, shifting, changing position, crossing and uncrossing them — and if I try to stop doing that, the feeling just builds up until I’m looking for some excuse to stand up or pace.

That’s honestly why I came in. I’ve been trying for months to just tough it out and sit there like I’m supposed to, but I still end up moving around anyway — shifting in my seat, pacing if I can get away with it, or finding some reason to get up even when I don’t really need to. It feels like my body won’t just let me sit still.
When you're trying to sit still, do you feel a specific discomfort or urge to move that starts in your legs, even before you feel the need to shift or get up?

I’m not totally sure I’d say it always starts in my legs specifically. Like, my legs are usually what gives me away first — I’ll start bouncing them or shifting them around, crossing and uncrossing, moving my feet — but the feeling itself is more like this whole-body restlessness.

It’s like when I’m in the radiology suite or sitting in a classroom and I know I’m supposed to stay put, I start feeling like I’m crawling out of my skin. I’ll try to sit there and ignore it, and I’ve tried to just tough it out for months, but it builds until I’m moving somehow. If I can’t get up, I’m shifting around in the chair. If I can get away with it, I’ll pace or find some excuse to move, even if I don’t really need to.

So, yes, there’s definitely an urge to move before I actually get up, but I don’t know if I’d describe it as only starting in my legs. It’s more like my body just won’t settle when I’m expected to sit still.

When you feel that restlessness and need to move, especially in situations where you’re supposed to sit still, do you also notice any unpleasant feelings in your legs — like tingling, crawling, or aching — that make you want to move them?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing it. Like, I wouldn’t say I get tingling or crawling feelings in my legs specifically, or aching that starts there and then I have to move them to make it stop.

It’s more like this general internal restlessness, like my body is wound up and sitting still makes it worse. My legs end up moving a lot because that’s the easiest thing to move when I’m stuck in a chair, but I haven’t really noticed a separate unpleasant leg sensation, if that makes sense. It’s not like my calves are hurting or buzzing or anything. It’s more just that I can’t settle.
Does this restlessness usually happen more in the evening or at night, or does it happen any time of day?

It’s not really just an evening or nighttime thing for me. I mean, I notice it whenever I’m in a situation where I’m supposed to sit still, like in the radiology suite or in class.

That’s kind of why I finally came in, honestly. It’s this feeling like I’m crawling out of my skin, and it can happen during the day if I’m stuck sitting and expected to stay put. I’ve tried for months to just tough it out and be still, but I still end up shifting around, pacing if I can, or finding some excuse to get up and move. So it feels more tied to having to sit still than to a specific time of day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms are most consistent with Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS), which is classified under ICD-10 as G25.81. The core features of RLS—an urge to move the legs, often accompanied by uncomfortable sensations, and a worsening of symptoms during rest or inactivity—are present. Although the patient describes a more 'whole-body' restlessness, the urge to move is clearly linked to periods of required immobility, and is relieved by movement, which aligns with RLS diagnostic criteria. ADHD (F90.0) was considered due to restlessness and difficulty staying still, but the absence of childhood onset, inattention, or impulsivity makes it less likely.
